lora_merge.Why merge a LoRA adapter before serving,: Unmerged, every call runs two extra small matmuls. Merged, the layer is a plain linear again, with zero added latency.
lora_merge.Why keep the adapter matrices after merg: Think about switching adapters on one base model, and about going back to training. PEFT keeps A and B so unmerge can restore W.
lora_merge.Write the merged weight in terms of W, A: W' = W + (alpha / r) B A. B is (out x r) and A is (r x in), so the product is (out x in), the same shape as W.
lora_merge.Why must the merge update the weight in: Optimizers, FSDP shards and tied weights hold a reference to the Parameter. Name what happens to them if you assign a new tensor, and what autograd would record without no_grad.
lora_merge.What happens if merge() is called twice,: Without a guard it adds the delta twice. A merged flag makes merge and unmerge idempotent.
lora_merge.Is merge then unmerge exact in bf16? Why: No: W + d - d is rounded twice in bf16 and can drift by an ulp per element. Mention casting the delta to the weight dtype and keeping an fp32 master copy.
lora_merge.Merged single-adapter serving versus unm: Merged: base-model latency, but one adapter per deployment. Unmerged: batched LoRA kernels serve many adapters over one base, at extra compute per token.
lora_merge.Can you merge a LoRA trained on a 4-bit: The adapter was trained against the dequantized base. Adding it to 4-bit weights forces a requantization, which loses most of the small delta.

dora.What is DoRA, and how does it differ fro: Write W as magnitude times unit direction per output row. LoRA updates the direction, and a separate trainable vector sets the magnitude.
dora.What do the magnitude vector and the dir: Magnitude is one length per output unit, and direction is W + delta W normalized per row. Count what the magnitude vector adds per layer.
dora.Along which axis is the weight norm take: Per output row of the (out x in) weight, i.e. norm over the input dimension. Each output unit gets its own scale.
dora.How must the magnitude be initialized so: Set m to the row norms of W. With B = 0, m / ||W|| is 1 and the output equals the base layer.
dora.Why does DoRA detach the norm in backwar: The paper's Section 4.3 treats ||W + delta W|| as a constant. Name the gradient term that drops and the activation memory it saves.
dora.How do you merge a trained DoRA adapter: The rescaled weight (m / ||W'||) W' is still one (out x in) matrix. Compute it once and write it into the base weight.
dora.DoRA versus LoRA at the same rank: accur: DoRA usually matches or beats LoRA accuracy at the same rank, but pays extra memory and time to rebuild W' and its norm each step.
dora.What does DoRA cost when the base model: The norm needs the full base weight, so each step dequantizes the 4-bit weights. Compare this with QLoRA, where only the matmul needs them.

prefix_tuning.What is prefix tuning, and how does it d: Prompt tuning adds trainable embeddings at the input only. Prefix tuning adds trainable keys and values in every layer, so it steers each attention layer directly.
prefix_tuning.What exactly is trained, and what shape: Only the prefix: per layer, a key and a value tensor of shape (heads, num_prefix, head_dim). The whole model stays frozen.
prefix_tuning.Why are the prefix keys and values not p: The prefix lives in key/value space already, like a KV cache. Projecting it again would tie it to frozen weights and change what it can express.
prefix_tuning.How do you build the attention mask once: Keys are prefix then tokens. Prefix columns are always visible; token column j is visible to query i if j <= i and token j is real.
prefix_tuning.Why can a naive lower-triangular mask ov: A tril over num_prefix + T hides later prefix slots from early queries. The prefix is a past that every query has already seen.
prefix_tuning.How does HuggingFace PEFT hand the prefi: It reshapes the prefix into per-layer (key, value) tensors and passes them as past_key_values. It also prepends ones to the attention mask, reusing the KV-cache code path.
prefix_tuning.Prefix tuning versus LoRA: trainable par: Prefix tuning trains fewer parameters but spends attention compute and cache on every step and cannot be merged. LoRA merges away and is usually more accurate.
prefix_tuning.Why does the original paper reparameteri: Training the prefix directly is unstable. The paper trains it through an MLP from a smaller embedding, then keeps only the MLP's output after training.
